A handful of common letters carry overloaded meanings in the literature. We enforce the following conventions throughout this paper to disambiguate them:

  • c = color (never charm; charm is \mathfrak{c}).

  • b = generic variable (never bottom quark; bottom is \mathfrak{b}).

  • p = brane point (never proton number; proton number is Z).

  • E alone = not used for an exceptional divisor, energy, or elliptic curve. We use \mathcal{S}_p, \mathfrak{E}, or \mathcal{E}_q respectively. E_{\mathfrak{H}} (with hadron subscript) is allowed for crossing energy.

  • \mathfrak{E}_0 vs Q_\beta(n) — two distinct hadronic-sector scalars historically conflated in Python compute scripts (see computations/binding_canonical.py history). They are not interchangeable:

    • \mathfrak{E}_0 = hadronic energy scale. We derive this as \mathfrak{E}_0^{(N=0)} = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) \approx 4.186 MeV (CAL-1 and CAL-2 only). The tower-summed form is \mathfrak{E}_0^{\text{full}} = \mathfrak{E}_0^{(N=0)}/(1-\hbar_q^2) \approx 4.228 MeV. It sets the MeV-per-dimensionless-trace-unit conversion for hadronic predictions.
    • Q_\beta(n) = 0.78233341\,\text{MeV} = the free-neutron \beta-decay Q-value. We derive this from CAL-2 (P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}). We use it as the binding-energy-scale multiplier in prop:categorical-mass-markov's explicit binding formula B = Q_\beta(n) \cdot (|\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}})| - |\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}})|). The ratio is \mathfrak{E}_0/Q_\beta(n) = 1/|\Delta(\mathrm{net})| \approx 5.31 (the dimensionless Hecke NF reduction). Code must name the parameter for the actual quantity it carries. Using E_0 for a Q_\beta-valued binding-scale variable is a registered notation violation.

  • \gamma = three reserved meanings, all standard, disambiguated by context: (i) the photon (default reading in particle / QED contexts: pair production \gamma\gamma \to e^+ e^-, photonic channels, Breit–Wheeler vertices); (ii) the Euler–Mascheroni constant (only inside zeta-value identities, e.g. \zeta'(0) = -\tfrac{1}{2}\log(2\pi), \gamma = \lim(H_n - \log n)); (iii) Dirac matrices \gamma^\mu (always with an explicit Lorentz index). We never use \gamma for a vortex or closed cycle — the vortex morphism is \varrho.

  • c_k vs \mathrm{cl}_k — the letter c carried three distinct coefficient families, two of them within ~12% of each other numerically, which is how they stayed conflated. We now split them:

    • c_k = Q_\beta precision-ladder coefficients only, Q_\beta = Q_{\text{base}}\prod_k(1 + c_k u^k) with u = b\hbar_q^2 — dimensionless, c_2 = -1, c_3 = -2 a near-match. (This register fixes the symbol; each rung's epistemic tier and its convention scoping live in the c_k/d_k canonical registry. The word "proved" previously appeared on c_2 here and is removed as a symbol-level claim — the Lean identity re-reads the N{=}2 factor rather than deriving it. "Taylor-exact" was NOT removed for being false, and must not be: c_2 genuinely is the u^2 coefficient of the explicit-factor product \prod_{k\ge2}(1 + c_k u^k). It is \tilde c_2 = -9/8 only for the normalised series with the cosine factor inside — so always say which series. No tier is changed by this edit.)
    • \tilde c_k = the normalised-series coefficients of the same ladder model: the u^k coefficients of \Phi(u)/\Phi(0) rather than of the explicit factors. The tilde marks a different normalisation of the same object — deliberately not justified by the old w_\lambda / \tilde w_\lambda pairing, which this same register retired in the entry below. The two families are not interchangeable: the model's cosine factor contributes at every order, and \tilde c_2 = c_2 - 1/8 exactly, independently of the phase \alpha (Lean, sorry-free: QOU.QBeta.normalisedQuadCoeff_eq), so the committed c_2 = -1 has \tilde c_2 = -9/8. Both are correct — one model at two normalisations. The -1/8 is contributed entirely by the half-argument in \cos(\alpha - u/2).
    • c_k^{\mathrm{even}} = the bar-even part of the ladder data, exact in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt 3) — a third object, read as neither c_k nor \tilde c_k.
    • \mathrm{cl}_k = cluster / Ursell coefficients of the many-body expansion — MeV-valued. \mathrm{cl}_3 = -\mathfrak{E}_0\,\Delta^2 g is the three-body cluster coefficient of the \mu_3 door (\mu_3 > 0 \iff \Delta^2 g < 0), and the Borromean H_9 magnitude lift is the same family. We never write a bare c_k for a cluster coefficient, and never quote a c_k value without saying which of c_k / \tilde c_k / c_k^{\mathrm{even}} it is — the three differ at the same k (-1, -9/8, \approx -8.006 at k = 2). Rationale for the roman two-letter tag rather than a new single letter: every single Roman letter is either register-claimed or produces a same-domain case-collision (X_k vs the knot object X_K; Y_k vs the Markov weight y_\lambda; Z = proton number; W_\lambda = geometric weight; j vs the Jones polynomial J_K(q)). This follows the same resolution already used for \mathrm{Sk} (Skein module, moved off \mathcal{S}) and h_{\mathrm{A}} (Hecke amplitude, moved off bare H_A).

  • \chi_q = Lyapunov exponent (distinct from \chi_\zeta(c), the character).

  • Euler characteristic is \chi_{\mathrm{eu}} — never a bare \chi. The glyph \chi is shared by three register-claimed families: the characters \chi_\lambda (Frobenius pairing \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda) and \chi_\zeta(c); the Lyapunov exponent \chi_q above; and the Euler characteristic, which keeps the standard glyph but always carries the roman subscript: \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}. A bare \chi is a notation violation in all three senses. When a total and its strata both appear we subscript further rather than overload: \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M) for the whole moduli, \chi_{\mathrm{eu},i} for the i-th Behrend stratum. The DT setting is where this bites — a Donaldson–Thomas count is a Behrend-weighted Euler characteristic \sum_i n_i\,\chi_{\mathrm{eu},i}, whose unweighted total \sum_i \chi_{\mathrm{eu},i} = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M) is a different number. (Write \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}, not an uppercase "\Chi": there is no such KaTeX/LaTeX macro — uppercase Greek chi is glyph-identical to Latin X and has no control sequence, so it fails the render gate. The orbifold Euler number of \Sigma(2,3,5) keeps its own conventional symbol e = -1/30.)

  • -2 vs -6 in the Stokes/DT sector — two integers that are not the same object and must not be swapped. \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3} \Delta_\lambda = -2 is the QOU Wedderburn/Springer Euler characteristic (partitionEuler3_eq) and is the prefactor of the GGM sandwich A \cdot W_{-1} \cdot B \cdot W_{-1}^{\mathsf{T}} \cdot C = -2\,S^{+}(0). The sandwich (0,1) entry is -6 = (-2)\cdot 3 — the prefactor times the Stokes/DT count S^{+}(0)_{01} = 3 — and is not an Euler characteristic, notwithstanding the G3 directive's "Euler = -6" hint. Cite -2 for the Euler characteristic and 3 for the count.

  • \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) names three different objects, and two corpus claims about it are in direct conflict — resolve the symbol to its object before quoting a value. Euler-characteristic stability fixes one bridge, \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(A_n) := \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_n}) = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}_n), the topological Euler characteristic of the total space. Three live sites then read it three ways. (i) Bring's Euler characteristic takes the generic fibre of \mathcal{S} to be Bring's surface \Sigma_4 and so reports -6. (ii) Quantum characteristic classes for SU(2) takes \mathcal{S} = \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1) \cong \mathbb{CP}^1 and so reports \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathbb{CP}^1) = 2. These are the same bridge applied to different \mathcal{S}, and the two disagree about the fibre — genus 4 against genus 0 — so at most one of them describes the state bundle of the Descartes universe. (iii) Knot-operator selection writes \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} \approx 2.0108968667 at the proton q_0. That is \dim_q of the fundamental V_1, not of the base algebra A = \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) — a third object, sharing only the glyph. The conflict is one of objects, not of notation. Substrate line bundle: base not fibre states that \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(A) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) is strictly independent of q, while lem:brings-euler-characteristic's own proof recovers the -6 as "the quantum dimension specialised at the Descartes substrate parameter q_0". A quantity independent of q does not need specialising at q_0, and reading (iii) is manifestly q-dependent. 🟧 OWNER RULING 2026-09-15 — reading (iii) is the categorical trace: \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) = \dim_q(A), the quantum dimension, which is the Euler characteristic of an object in the QOU category. Verbatim: "i think it is [2]_q ... euler characteristic of object in the QOU category". Three consequences, and the first two are corrections to live blocks. (1) \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) is q-DEPENDENT. So substrate line bundle: base not fibre's bullet — "\chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(A) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) is strictly independent of q" — is withdrawn. Its four sibling bullets (\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)), c_1, c_2, the Euler class e(\xi)) are untouched; only the trace bullet moves. (2) The integers -6 and 2 are TOPOLOGICAL Euler characteristics \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}), a different object from the categorical trace. They are therefore not competing values of one quantity, and neither is "wrong" — but Euler-characteristic stability's bridge \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_n}) = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}_n) is now a substantive claim relating two different things, not a restatement: it equates a q-dependent quantity with a q-independent integer, so it can hold at most on a locus in q unless a regularisation is supplied. Whether that locus contains q_0 is open. (3) lem:brings-euler-characteristic's proof is now in the right register, and the ruling FORCES a regularisation on it. Its "the quantum dimension of A specialises at q_0 to -6" is the correct kind of statement under the ruling. Measured, exact mpf at 50 dps (trace_id_quantum_dimension_probe.py, 8/8): \dim_q(V_n) = [n+1]_q is positive and strictly increasing, with infimum [1]_q = 1, so -6 is not the naive quantum dimension of any finite-dimensional irrep. But the sharper fact is about A itself. A = \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is not an irrep — by Peter–Weyl it is \bigoplus_n V_n \otimes V_n^{*}, so its naive quantum dimension is \sum_n [n+1]_q^2, whose terms grow like q^{2n}. At q_0 > 1 that diverges: consecutive-term ratio 1.23205245417 at n = 120, partial sum already 1.12 \times 10^{13}. So the naive \dim_q(A) is not a real number at q_0 at all — a regularisation is not an optional refinement of the -6 reading, it is required before \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) has a value, and the ruling is what forces that. Alternating sums over the same tower do reach negatives (\sum_{k=0}^{3} (-1)^k [k+1]_q = -2.0769), which is the shape a -6 would have to come from; that the corpus's -6 arises that way is not claimed. Scope (b) for the divergence, invariant = a series with consecutive-term ratio above 1; scope (a) for the rest. The Lean carrier settles none of it: climax-volume-mass/vertex-algebra-relations.lean asserts \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}) = -6 as an axiom, over a MarkovTrace that is itself an axiom, for every strand count and every parameter — assumption on assumption, which per §"Axiomatization is NOT a Proof" is not a derivation, and which under this ruling is now also wrong in q-dependence. Cite a value with its object, never a bare \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A). Bean qou-2uf0. 🟧 RESOLVED 2026-09-15 (owner selection: separate by name; both objects, distinct symbols). Four symbols, never interchanged: \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) is the topological Euler characteristic of the base curve (the -6; three Euler characteristics); \chi(M_0, V), always with two arguments, is the sheaf Euler characteristic h^0 - h^1 of a bundle on the base (Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch; equals \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) only when \mathrm{rk}\, V = 2 and \deg V = 0); \dim_q(X) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_X) is the rigid trace of an object of \mathbf{C}, so \dim_q(V) = [2]_q for the fundamental object and \dim_q(A) for the Frobenius–Hopf object is a regularised quantity, written \dim_q^{\zeta}(A) when the scheme matters, equal to 0 = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) under \zeta-regularisation (regular representation); and w(A) is the obstruction class of the Wigner axiom, whose archimedean image is the Euler class e(\xi). A bare \chi(A) is retired. Collisions checked: the Hecke characters \chi_\lambda carry a partition subscript, the Lyapunov exponent \chi_q carries q, the motivic measure is \chi_{\mathrm{top}} (its own entry), and the Euler characteristics carry roman \mathrm{eu} or two arguments, so no two of these can be confused by glyph alone. Options that were considered and not taken: \chi_{\mathrm{hol}}(V) or \mathrm{ind}\,\bar\partial_V for the sheaf Euler characteristic (the two-argument form keeps the standard glyph and reads correctly to the audience), and \mathrm{sdim}_q for the regularised trace (the superscript scheme is more honest, since the value depends on it).

  • \theta_p vs \vartheta_K — two unrelated objects sharing a glyph. \theta_p(w) = \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} p^{-n(n+1)/2}w^{n} is the q-theta of a q-difference operator: a function of a complex variable, satisfying \theta_p(pw) = w\,\theta_p(w), whose zero set is the orbit -p^{\mathbb{Z}}. \vartheta_K is the angular deformation parameter of the volume channel S_K = A_\omega\,\kappa\,(\ln^{2} q_0 - \vartheta_K^{2}) — a real angle attached to a knot, not a function. Neither is a Newton-polygon slope; "theta order" in the slope register is a third, again unrelated, use of the word.

  • \Omega_q = the Reeb period only. This is one object across two regimes: in the finite categorical model it is the smallest positive integer with \xi_q^{\Omega_q} = \mathrm{id}_A (def:categorical-reeb-derivation, Lean field period : ℕ; the divisibility 6 \mid \Omega_q is an integer-regime statement only), and at the substrate it is the infinite surreal \Omega_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-1} \asymp \omega (surreal rate calculus). These are the same period lifted, not a collision. What is not \Omega_q: the q-deformed Kerov limit-shape space — the target of the Plancherel pushforwards \iota_n — is \mathcal{K}_q (calligraphic, per the space convention; was written \Omega_q before, colliding with the period). A topological space is not a period; do not carry 6 \mid \Omega_q to \mathcal{K}_q or to the surreal. The q-oper datum \Omega^1_q (a differential, q-geometric-langlands) is a superscripted third use and unrelated; its tensor powers keep the superscript, (\Omega^1_q)^{\otimes 2}, never a bare \Omega_q^{\otimes 2} (which reads as a power of the period). A fourth use is claimed and is disambiguated by its argument, in the manner of \zeta(s) and H_q(\lambda) above: \Omega_q(\varrho) is the q-holonomy residue of a loop \varrho, an element of \mathrm{End}(\tau(\mathcal{L}_q)) fixed by \mathcal{L}_q(\varrho) = \mathrm{id} + (q-1)\Omega_q(\varrho) (def:q-local-system). It is an endomorphism, not a number: the divisibility 6 \mid \Omega_q does not reach it either. Never write it without its loop argument.

  • \zeta = three distinct uses, never bare. We use \zeta_n := e^{2\pi i/n} (primitive n-th root of unity, always with integer subscript — e.g. \zeta_5, \zeta_6 = e^{i\pi/3}); \zeta(s) (Riemann zeta function, always parenthesised, e.g. \zeta(2) = \pi^2/6, \zeta(3) — Apéry's constant); \chi_\zeta(c) (character, always with \chi prefix and argument). We do not use the bare token \zeta alone.

  • \mathcal{P}_n = Goncharov period filtration class (weight-n periods modulo lower-weight). This is distinct from P_\ell, the elementary symmetric polynomials in Jucys–Murphy elements (prop:jucys-murphy-central-elements-qou), which are non-calligraphic and indexed by symmetric-polynomial degree.

  • H_q alone = not used. Three distinct concepts share the letter H: \mathcal{H}_q (shuffle Hopf algebra), \hat{H}_q (Hamiltonian operator), H_n(q) or H_q(\lambda) (Hecke / hook-length, always with argument). The Hecke amplitude q - q^{-1} is h_{\mathrm{A}} (plain-italic scalar, roman subscript). Older text splits this between "\mathrm{HA}" and a bare "H_A"; bare H_A collided with the Hecke algebra H_A(q) on A strands.

  • W alone = not used. Two unrelated objects claim the bare letter: the rank-2 Hodge plane of H^1(\text{Bring}) = 2W, which carries the three calibrations (three-calibration discipline), and the three-dimensional object with irreducible \mathrm{Sym}^2 that the eightfold way is missing (eightfold open problems). We write the first only as 2W or as the rank-2 W-plane, and the second only with its dimension stated, so that no occurrence relies on the reader's context. The decorated forms are separately claimed and are neither of these: W_\lambda (geometric weight), W(\gamma) (abstract Wilson-loop functional; the confinement observable is \mathfrak{W}), W(A_2) (Weyl group, always with a root system as argument), and W_{\text{free}} / W_{\text{atom}} (braid words in the binding formula above).

  • \mathrm{SU}(3) alone = permitted only for a representation-theoretic statement true of any \mathrm{SU}(3) (e.g. "\mathbf{3}\otimes\bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8}\oplus\mathbf{1} is standard \mathrm{SU}(3) representation theory"). The two groups the paper actually uses are distinct and are always subscripted: \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} (colour — the stabiliser \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} \subset G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}), the colour tubes, the gluon octet) and \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} (flavour — the group organising the meson/baryon octets, the decuplet, and quark flavour). Roman lowercase subscripts, matching h_{\mathrm{A}} and \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}. The reason is that the eightfold-way open-problems block asks, as its item 4, whether the two are the same, different, or groupoid-dual; a shared glyph presupposes an answer. A sentence that deliberately compares them carries both subscripts. Legacy spellings elsewhere in the corpus — \mathrm{SU}(3)_c, \mathrm{SU}(3)_L, \mathrm{SU}(3)_R (chiral, in the colour-superconductivity observation) and SU(3)_color in audit documents — are recorded here as legacy and are not swept by this ruling.

  • \mathfrak{S} = categorical action (fraktur, Hamilton's S). We previously wrote the action two ways — calligraphic \mathcal{S}_q and plain S_q. We now unify both to \mathfrak{S}_q throughout the paper. This frees calligraphic \mathcal{S} for the state bundle alone (QOU tuple (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S})). Three other objects deliberately keep S / \mathrm{Sk} and are not the action:

    • the Hopf antipode S (plain S, or S_q on the q-shuffle Hopf algebra);
    • the q-entropy S_q(U) (quantum-temperature, with \partial S_q/\partial \mathfrak{E}_q = 1/T_q) and the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy S_{BH} — entropy is a distinct thermodynamic observable, never the action;
    • the Skein module \mathrm{Sk}_q(\mathbf{C}) — the \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]-algebra of knot classes, with mass functional \mathfrak{m}\colon \mathrm{Sk}_q \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} (fraktur; the calligraphic \mathcal{M} is reserved for the mass endomorphism \mathcal{M}(K)\in\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(X_K) — see the \mathcal{M} ruling below). We moved the Skein module off calligraphic \mathcal{S} (where it collided with the state bundle) to roman \mathrm{Sk}, since single-letter calligraphic was blocked: \mathcal{S} = state bundle, \mathcal{K} = knot.

  • \mathfrak{O} = observation / intent morphism — the section (\mathfrak{O}, \epsilon) of \mathrm{Ad}(J^1\mathcal{S}) and its germ endomorphism \mathfrak{O}_p. We never use this for an ideal. The genus-filtration ideal keeps \mathfrak{I} (\mathfrak{I}_4 = (u^5)). We moved intent off \mathfrak{I} to disambiguate the two.

  • \mathfrak{W} = confinement observable / q-Wilson loop \mathfrak{W}(\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{T}). We never use this for the observation morphism (now \mathfrak{O}). The abstract Wilson-loop functional is plain W(\gamma). This is distinct from \mathfrak{V} (below).

  • \mathbb{M}_{n,q} = the q-Plancherel measure on partitions of n, \mathbb{M}_{n,q}(\lambda) = q^{n(\lambda)} f^\lambda / \prod_\square \{h(\square)\}_q with the asymmetric q-integers \{k\}_q = (q^k-1)/(q-1) (prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton). Blackboard bold for the same reason as \mathbb{V} above — it is the source literature's own symbol and both cheaper glyphs are taken: plain M is the (deprecated) base manifold and appears as \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M), and \mathcal{M} is the mass endomorphism, which the \mathcal{M} ruling below forbids overloading. Three distinct things are NOT this measure and must not be written \mathbb{M}: the Wedderburn weight w_\lambda = \dim_q^2/[n]_q! (a different measure — it disagrees with \mathbb{M}_{n,q^2} by a relative 978 at n=12, and is not even normalised), the Markov weights y_\lambda, and the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M, whose subscript M is Markov and is unrelated. Note also that n(\lambda) = \sum_i (i-1)\lambda_i is Macdonald's statistic, not a function of the size n; the size is always the bare n. The corpus's Molien / fake-degree weight is this same measure at Q = q^2 — exactly, probes/molien_feray_meliot_bridge_probe.py — so a claim proved for one holds for the other and neither transfers to w_\lambda.

  • \mathfrak{V} = the complex-volume observable (QOU analogue of the Neumann–Zagier complex volume \mathbb{V}=\mathrm{Vol}+i\,\mathrm{CS}): \mathfrak{V}(K) = E_0\,\mathrm{tr}_M((\Pi_{\text{free}}-\mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M}). Its real part is binding \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} = \mathrm{Re}\mathfrak{V} (bar-even / \cosh) and its imaginary part is the \beta-decay Q-value \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V} (bar-odd / \sinh) (conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume). We do not use \mathfrak{W} (Wilson loop) or \mathbb{V} (the literal NZ symbol, used only as the analogy reference).

  • \Pi_{\text{free}} = idempotent projector onto the factorized sub-object (parabolic/Young subalgebra; constituents un-linked). The "free" trace is \mathrm{tr}_M\circ\Pi_{\text{free}}.

  • \mathfrak{Q}_\beta (fraktur) = the \beta-decay Q-value as a trace-component (\mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V}, derived). We promoted this to fraktur (observable register) from the older roman Q_\beta. The measured/experimental value is \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\,\mathrm{obs}} (CODATA).

  • \mathfrak{D} (decay width) vs \mathcal{D} (operator) — visually close but register-distinct. We write \mathfrak{D} (fraktur, a genuine decay-rate observable) always carrying a decay subscript — \mathfrak{D}_n (neutron), \mathfrak{D}_\mu (muon), \mathfrak{D}_K (generic hadron) — under the convention \mathfrak{D}_K = \hbar/\tau_K. The calibration channels P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} (CAL-2) and P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi} (CAL-3) formerly carried this symbol and no longer do: they are bar-parity projections, not rates, and their proxies are a Q-value and a mass respectively. We write \mathcal{D} (calligraphic, an operator) as the categorical Dirac operator \mathcal{D}_\nabla or the path measure \mathcal{D}\phi. The subscript / decoration disambiguates. We never write a bare \mathfrak{D} or bare \mathcal{D}.

  • S_n vs H_n(q) — q-deformed braiding decompositions (eigenvalues \{q, -q^{-1}\}) are actions of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q), not the symmetric group S_n, even when the block dimensions match the classical S_n irreps. We write classical S_n only for a genuine \epsilon = \pm 1 flip. We never write fraktur \mathfrak{S}_n (fraktur \mathfrak{S} is the action).

  • "depth" = six distinct filtration/cutoff indices share this English word, and the register had never claimed it — which is why the name stayed available to be taken repeatedly. We never write a bare "depth"; each sense carries its own symbol and is named in full on first use in a block.

    • transcendence depth n — the iterated-integral index of \mathcal{H}_q^{(n,K)}, where G^{(n)} adjoins \mathrm{Li}_n^q and \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}) \subseteq \mathcal{P}_n. This is the sense moved additively by the q-shuffle (\mathcal{H}^{(n_1)} \ast_q \mathcal{H}^{(n_2)} \subseteq \bigoplus \mathcal{H}^{(n_1+n_2)}), and the sense the K-theory period rosetta indexes.

    • cell \lambda_K \vdash n_K — the Hecke/knot partition cell of an atom's braid. A partition, not an integer; write the partition, never "the depth of K".

    • curvature-rank k — the Gröbner–Shirshov grading, k = \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) - 1 with \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) the partition depth (max hook length). Read the scope note: all three readings of the underlying J^\bullet are excluded (bean qou-wjbd), so this index is currently attached to no well-defined filtration. Renaming it does not supply one.

    • cascade depth N_{\mathrm{eff}} = \lfloor \log_q(\mathrm{Re}_q^{3/4}) \rfloor — the q-turbulence Reynolds cutoff of the fluid-dynamics chapter. Not a filtration at all, and unrelated to every sense above.

    • triangulation size n — the number of ideal tetrahedra in a hyperbolic triangulation of the \Phi_q-piece K_S. This is the sense the pole-to-cusp correspondence counts: conj:shared-denominator-cusp-holonomy's table row 4 reads "n ideal tetrahedra in JSJ piece", and computations/snappy_cusp_seeding.py takes n from SnapPy's num_tetrahedra() and emits one algebraic seed per tetrahedron — eight for the eight-tetrahedron \mathtt{L6a4}, not three for its three cusps. It collides head-on with the GB-depth k_\star(T_w) = n that the same conjecture's own hypothesis fixes, and with transcendence depth n above: for the figure-eight 4_1 the triangulation has 2 tetrahedra and 1 cusp, while the braid whose closure it is, (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^2, lives in H_3(q) (computations/eigenvalue_reeb_extension_h4_h5.py, atom-word-braid-letter-census.witness.json). The corpus asserts the first two are equal — thurston-relaxation calls it the "GB-PL bijection" — and names no carrier at all for it: that parenthetical is bare prose, with no label and no link of its own, so the assertion cannot be reached by grepping for any block. Scoped on an owner ruling, 2026-10-10: that line now says the identification is asserted rather than established and carries the tier of conj:algebraic-geometric-dilog-equivalence, whose clause (1) rests on it. Read the link that now appears there carefully — it points at the conjecture that depends on the identification, not at a carrier for it, so the absence this entry records is unchanged. The label the dated audits record for it, prop:jet-gb-pl-correspondence, resolves to no file in the tree (and to no witness: the jet-gb-pl-correspondence.witness.json that docs/audits/2026-05-18-compute-integration-sweep.md lists is absent too); both audits place it at content/quantum-observable-universe/descartes-universe/, a directory that no longer exists. So the identification is currently unsupported rather than merely unproved — the ruling scoped how it is stated, and decided no mathematics — and this entry is the only live site that names the label, which it does solely to record the absence. Never write a bare n in this arc.

    • tower depth N — the brane-tower truncation index, as in \mathfrak{E}_0^{(N)} and N_v = 120\,q_0^{90}. This is the one sense the register already carried, inside the energy row of the fraktur table, where nothing marked it as a claim on the word.

Bar-even / bar-odd: always the coefficient half

The words bar-even and bar-odd label four different gradings in this paper. They are not four involutions. All four descend from the single def:bar-involution on H_n(q),

  \overline{\sigma_i} = \sigma_i^{-1}, \qquad \overline{q} = q^{-1},

which has two halves that blocks apply independently:

Half Acts by Geometrically
coefficient half q \mapsto q^{-1}, diagram fixed reciprocates the weights
diagram half \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, coefficients fixed the mirror: exchanges positive and negative crossings, p \leftrightarrow m

Convention. In this paper bar-even and bar-odd always mean parity under the coefficient half. A parity taken under the diagram half is called mirror-even / mirror-odd, never "bar-". Which grading is meant:

Splits Graded by Where
A the Laurent scalar \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} into \cosh\lambda / \sinh\lambda coefficient half obs:crossing-energy-decomposition
B the Hecke module into e_+ / e_- by eigenvalue q / -q^{-1} neither — the full involution fixes both idempotents prop:em-coupling-projection
C the knot, by the mirror; the channel totals E_{\mathrm{sym}} / E_{\mathrm{asym}} diagram half same block as A, item 2
D the algebra A = A_+ \oplus A_- by the spin involution coefficient half def:spin-involution

A and D are the same grading. On the symmetric/alternating Hecke block the spin involution acts as the eigenvalue swap q^{2k} \leftrightarrow q^{-2k}, which is exactly the coefficient half; its sectors are A_+ = \cosh(2k\lambda) and A_- = \sinh(2k\lambda). So A_+ bar-even and A_- bar-odd agrees with \cosh\lambda bar-even and \sinh\lambda bar-odd, and the shared vocabulary is consistent rather than colliding.

C is anti-correlated with A, and this is not an error. The weight \cosh\lambda is bar-even, while its channel total E_{\mathrm{sym}} = (p - m)\cosh\lambda is mirror-odd, because the mirror flips the multiplicity p - m as well as the weight. Both statements hold of the same summand; only the half differs. Read a parity claim about a weight as coefficient-half and a parity claim about a channel total as diagram-half unless the text says otherwise.

Never say "bar-even" unqualified of a channel. Under the full involution both crossing-energy channels are negated, and both Hecke idempotents are fixed, so the words separate nothing there. They are informative only relative to a named half. Proved sorry-free over a general field in QOU.BraidKnot.CrossingEnergyBarParity (eSym_coef, eSym_mirror, bar_neg_of_both); the full atlas including gradings B and D is bar-parity-involution-atlas.witness.json.

Four different objects wear the glyph \sigma — the Hecke generator \sigma_i, the mirror K \mapsto K^{\sigma}, the spin involution \sigma : A \to A, and the bar involution itself, which several blocks write as \sigma \colon q \mapsto q^{-1}. A bare \sigma therefore never disambiguates a parity claim; name the half instead.

That last usage carries its own hazard: writing the bar involution as "\sigma \colon q \mapsto q^{-1}" states only the coefficient half, and a reader who takes it as the definition will compute the wrong parity for anything living inside H_n(q). Three corpus claims have been caught by exactly this slip: the crossing-energy channels and the V_\lambda \leftrightarrow V_{\lambda'} intertwiner (which is the sign twist \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1}, not the bar involution) are corrected here, and the argument from bar-invariance for the Markov parameter z is withdrawn — its bar-partner is z - h, not z, because M3 contains \sigma_n. (The z convention is settled independently of this: convention D, z = q^3/(q^2+1), is canonical and C is excised; see def:markov-axioms-primitive.) When the object being graded lies in the algebra, use both halves.

QCD vocabulary: five words that mean something else here

Every collision above is internal — two objects inside this framework wearing one glyph. This section records a different hazard: five terms that carry a standard meaning in QCD and a different, unrelated meaning in this corpus. The risk is not that an author confuses two of our own objects, but that a reader — or an agent asked whether the framework speaks to some measurement — greps for the QCD term, finds hundreds of files, and concludes the topic is covered.

Term Standard QCD meaning What it means in this corpus
saturation small-x gluon recombination; the saturation scale Q_s(x) three unrelated things: the genus saturation of T_{2,9}; nuclear saturation, meaning the B/A plateau (QOU.Mass.CoordinationSaturation); and "scales saturate" in the cosmological limits
shadowing nuclear shadowing; Gribov inelastic screening LP-dual shadow prices y_0^{\star}, y^{\star} — the binding-energy duals of prop:operator-selection-lp. Also "archimedean shadow" and the a_1 "parity shadow"
diffraction Pomeron exchange; diffractive dissociation optical diffraction — Fraunhofer, Airy, the double-slit chapter
S-matrix the scattering matrix the modular S-matrix of a modular tensor category — the Reshetikhin–Turaev / Chern–Simons vacuum row and total quantum dimension D = \sum_i d_i^2
Fourier transform conjugate to momentum or impact parameter the discrete transform on C_n (Lagrange resolvent), the categorical Fourier transform, and the adelic one. None is a transform over a transverse plane

What this framework does not have, measured rather than inferred. The following carry zero occurrences across content/, docs/ and computations/: parton, Bjorken, DGLAP, deep inelastic, photoproduction, nuclear shadowing, Mandelstam, impact parameter, transverse plane, momentum space. The framework evaluates its observables at a single substrate modulus and produces knot invariants, not amplitudes differential in momentum transfer.

Why the list is stated as a rule and not as a search result. Two of the five — S-matrix and Fourier transform — were about to be reported absent from this corpus on the strength of a topic grep that returned nothing for the QCD sense. They are present in over a hundred files each, meaning something else entirely. A topic grep answers "does this word occur", never "does this concept occur", and the gap between those two questions is exactly where a false negative and a false positive can be produced from the same evidence.

Related: the bare-\sigma hazard above, and the three distinct partition-weight families in notation-register.md, are the internal instances of the same discipline — resolve a name to its definition before reasoning about what it denotes.

"One-dimensional": four senses, and the spatial one is the rarest

A word collision rather than a glyph collision, and the reason it is recorded here is the reverse of the usual one: the corpus is mostly already unambiguous, and the hazard is an agent concluding otherwise from a raw count.

Four unrelated senses share the phrase.

  • Representation dimension — a Wedderburn block, irrep or character of dimension one; a one-row or one-column Young diagram.
  • Linear-algebraic dimension — a solution space, a cohomology group, a module of forms: "HH^2 \cong k is one-dimensional", "\Lambda^2 H^* is one-dimensional".
  • Seminormal channel dimension — the channel on which a generator acts by a scalar (AlphaShiftOneDimChannel). Both Lean files whose names contain OneDimChannel are this sense or the one above, not the spatial one.
  • Spatial dimension — \dim M_k = 1: the descent stratum, the linear layout, the filament.

Measured (773 occurrences across content/, the Lean tree, computations/ and docs/; one_dimensional_sense_audit.py): 526 carry a disambiguating noun immediately after the phrase — block, channel, representation, character, irrep, Wedderburn — and are not ambiguous to anyone. Of the 254 bare uses, the overwhelming majority are clear from their own sentence, and the genuinely spatial bare uses number about four.

The authoring rule, which is about new writing rather than a sweep. Write the spatial sense as \dim M_k = d, or qualify it in words as spatially one-dimensional / one spatial dimension. It is the rarest sense by more than an order of magnitude, so a bare "one-dimensional" in new prose will be read as one of the other three. The other senses need no change: they are already carried by the noun, and rewriting them would be churn.

Do not repeat the alarmist reading. The 773 figure, and a classifier bucket labelled "unclassified", were both produced in this corpus and both invite the conclusion that the phrase is pervasively ambiguous. They do not support it — "unclassified" there means the classifier's regex had no marker, not that a reader cannot tell. Three separate samples of that bucket turned out to be plainly clear linear-algebraic and representation uses. If you re-measure, count the bare uses whose own sentence leaves the sense open; that number is small.
